brief.scope: The fixture apps batch, slice 5 (apps/rust-crate), the skeptic pass: judge the test on this ref against the contract in the input file (the fixture scope and the plan for slices 3 to 5; the slice 5 section). The test is landed on this ref, red first: ops/devlane/fixtures/tests/test_rust_crate_app.py, proving the crate through the merged lever ops/bin/fixture.sh (make, prove red on every planted fault and green on every clean neighbour, prove --fixed green, the manifest sweep, grade) with the toolchain the plan names (cargo offline, the warm registry). Judge whether it discriminates, whether every fault the plan assigns is pinned with its span and probe, whether the probes prove red mechanically, and whether a wrong crate or a wrong FAULTS.json would pass. No implementation exists yet; do not write one.

findings.claim: RC-01 through RC-06 are not pinned to their exact shell gates, Cargo targets, or behavioral probes. The suite only runs manifest-supplied commands and observes exit status before and after manifest-supplied patches. A wrong crate using static greps over planted marker comments, empty probe targets, and patches deleting those comments would pass RED, GREEN, isolation, and reset without proving any assigned behavior.

The binary contract is untested. src/main.rs need only exist and compile; no assertion runs the read/write verbs, requires WF_AGENT for writes, or verifies exit classes and the expected-found-needed refusal line. An empty fn main() {} would pass when the library fixtures and dummy integration tests satisfy the remaining checks.

A wrong FAULTS.json can choose its own oracle. The test pins only each location path, not its function or lines, exact practiced and declared quotations, finding text, neighbour span, probe path, or fix path. Broad dirty and clean regexes can match comments, while the generic sweep merely verifies self-chosen quotations at self-chosen spans, corrupting calibration without failing.
findings.reproduce: python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; s=Path("ops/devlane/fixtures/tests/test_rust_crate_app.py").read_text(); print({k:(k in s) for k in ["EXPECTED_LOCATION_LINES","EXPECTED_PRACTICED","EXPECTED_PROBES","EXPECTED_FIXES","EXPECTED_NEIGHBOURS","row.get(\"declared\")","row.get(\"practiced\")","row.get(\"finding\")"]})'

findings.claim: RC-07 can remain unpinned after its fix. Replacing anyhow = "*" with a compatible range such as anyhow = "^1" makes the planned wildcard grep green and can leave cargo test --locked green. No post-fix assertion requires an exact =<Cargo.lock version> dependency.

The manifest toolchain and check commands can be inert strings. Unanchored keyword checks accept quoted no-ops; install and ready are never executed from the manifest, and a check such as : 'cargo fmt clippy cargo test --offline --locked' matches every assertion and exits zero. Hard-coded private Cargo invocations do not prove the advertised manifest interface.
